title: Shredded Chicken Quesadillas
subtitle: Melty, crispy, line-friendly
description: Melty, crispy, line-friendly. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Shredded Chicken Quesadillas in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on. Use Ground beef, Yellow onion, Garlic cloves as listed — measure each before heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch chicken. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Cook and sauce filling
steps.instruction: Slow-cook or simmer filling until shreddable (pork 203°F, meatballs cooked through). Simmer in sauce 15 minutes so flavor penetrates. Target 165°F at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Toast buns
steps.instruction: Toast split buns on a dry griddle until golden. Melt cheese on top if desired. Cook until char marks are visible and the thickest piece reads 165°F on an instant-read thermometer. Plan about 6 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Build the sandwich line
steps.instruction: Shredded Chicken Quesadillas on sheet trays: bottom bun, meat, sauce, cheese, top bun. Serve immediately; hold wrapped sandwiches at 200°F up to 20 minutes.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Shredded Chicken Quesadillas onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Scale for larger halls
steps.instruction: When cooking for more than 8 firefighters, split into two pans halfway through so the bottom layer does not overcook while the top waits — duplicate mise en place if you double batches.

steps.title: Hold for late calls
steps.instruction: Keep backup sandwiches foil-wrapped at 200°F. Slice hoagies in half for easier grabbing — crew eats with one hand when tones are quiet.

steps.title: Final quality check before service
steps.instruction: Walk the line once before opening service for Shredded Chicken Quesadillas — confirm hotel pans are labeled, backup trays are in the 200°F oven, and thermometers are calibrated. Rookies should ask a senior cook to spot-check the first portion.

steps.instruction: Walk the line once before opening service for Shredded Chicken Quesadillas — confirm hotel pans are labeled, backup trays are in the 200°F oven, and thermometers are calibrated. Rookies should ask a senior cook to spot-check the first portion.

proTips: Prep all mise en place before the bell — this meal wins on organization, not speed hacks.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
Pull chicken at 160°F and let carryover hit 165°F — dry breast ruins crew morale.
tonightSpread: Plate Shredded Chicken Quesadillas with sides in separate pans so the crew can mix portions.
Line up Shredded Chicken Quesadillas on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Melty, crispy, line-friendly. A hall pick for tight shifts — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
mealPrepNotes: Minimal prep — chop aromatics before shift change so you can cook as soon as the board quiets.
substitutions: Chicken thighs ↔ breasts (thighs forgive overcooking on the flat-top).
